You are implementing ONE requirement in the Apache Hadoop source tree at /workspace (a real upstream repo checked out at an earlier state).

REQUIREMENT SLUG: distcp-typos
REQUIREMENT FILE: /workspace/requirements/distcp-typos.yaml   <-- READ THIS FIRST

The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree. Hidden tests derived from the real upstream commit will grade the result, so EXACT naming matters:
  * new/changed configuration keys and their default values (and their entries in *-default.xml)
  * new class / interface / method / field / metric names and their visibility
  * log message wording and format placeholders
  * behavioural details (return values, exception types, ordering, off-by-one boundaries)
If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. Some modules have a TestYarnConfigurationFields / TestHdfsConfigFields style test that requires the xml and the constant to agree - keep them in sync.
5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.
6. Do NOT run maven/mvn or cmake (there is no warm build environment; it wastes your time). Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.
7. Scope discipline: change ONLY what this requirement needs. Do not reformat unrelated lines, do not fix unrelated warnings, do not touch other subsystems. Other agents are concurrently implementing ~380 other requirements in this same working tree.

FORBIDDEN COMMANDS (they would destroy other agents' concurrent work): git checkout / switch / stash / reset / revert / clean / rebase / merge / cherry-pick, `git add -A` or `git add .` without an explicit pathspec, `git commit --amend`, `git rm` of files you did not create, and any `mvn`/`gradle` invocation.

WHEN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE - commit it yourself with exactly this shape (substitute the real repo-relative paths you touched, space separated, and keep the flock):

  cd /workspace && flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c 'git add -A -- PATH1 PATH2 ... && git diff --cached --binary > requirement_patches/distcp-typos.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: distcp-typos" && git log --oneline -1 && wc -c requirement_patches/distcp-typos.diff'

Rules for that step:
  * List every file you created, modified or deleted as an explicit pathspec. Never a bare directory like `.`.
  * requirement_patches/distcp-typos.diff MUST come out non-empty (wc -c > 0). If `git commit` reports "nothing to commit", another agent already committed your lines: verify the requirement is genuinely satisfied in the working tree, then report that in your notes.
  * Do not touch requirement_patches/ for any other slug.

FINALLY return ONLY a JSON object (this is your return value, not a message to a human):
{"slug":"distcp-typos","status":"done"|"partial"|"blocked","files":["..."],"committed":true|false,"patch_bytes":<int>,"summary":"<=3 sentences on what you changed","notes":"anything the orchestrator must know (conflicts, follow-ups, uncertainty)"}

1 14 15 #set ( $H3 = '###' ) 16 #set ( $H4 = '####' ) 17 18 DistCp Guide 19 ===================== 20 21 --- 22 23 - [Overview](#Overview) 24 - [Usage](#Usage) 25 - [Basic Usage](#Basic_Usage) 26 - [Update and Overwrite](#Update_and_Overwrite) 27 - [Sync](#Sync) 28 - [Command Line Options](#Command_Line_Options) 29 - [Architecture of DistCp](#Architecture_of_DistCp) 30 - [DistCp Driver](#DistCp_Driver) 31 - [Copy-listing Generator](#Copy-listing_Generator) 32 - [InputFormats and MapReduce Components](#InputFormats_and_MapReduce_Components) 33 - [Appendix](#Appendix) 34 - [Map sizing](#Map_sizing) 35 - [Copying Between Versions of HDFS](#Copying_Between_Versions_of_HDFS) 36 - [MapReduce and other side-effects](#MapReduce_and_other_side-effects) 37 - [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently_Asked_Questions) 38 39 --- 40 41 Overview 42 -------- 43 44 DistCp (distributed copy) is a tool used for large 45 inter/intra-cluster copying. It uses MapReduce to effect its distribution, 46 error handling and recovery, and reporting. It expands a list of files and 47 directories into input to map tasks, each of which will copy a partition of 48 the files specified in the source list. 49 50 [The erstwhile implementation of DistCp] 51 (http://hadoop.apache.org/docs/r1.2.1/distcp.html) has its share of quirks 52 and drawbacks, both in its usage, as well as its extensibility and 53 performance. The purpose of the DistCp refactor was to fix these 54 shortcomings, enabling it to be used and extended programmatically. New 55 paradigms have been introduced to improve runtime and setup performance, 56 while simultaneously retaining the legacy behaviour as default. 57 58 This document aims to describe the design of the new DistCp, its spanking new 59 features, their optimal use, and any deviance from the legacy implementation. 60 61 Usage 62 ----- 63 64 $H3 Basic Usage 65 66 The most common invocation of DistCp is an inter-cluster copy: 67 68 bash$ hadoop distcp hdfs://nn1:8020/foo/bar \ 69 hdfs://nn2:8020/bar/foo 70 71 This will expand the namespace under `/foo/bar` on nn1 into a temporary file, 72 partition its contents among a set of map tasks, and start a copy on each 73 NodeManager from `nn1` to `nn2`. 74 75 One can also specify multiple source directories on the command line: 76 77 bash$ hadoop distcp hdfs://nn1:8020/foo/a \ 78 hdfs://nn1:8020/foo/b \ 79 hdfs://nn2:8020/bar/foo 80 81 Or, equivalently, from a file using the -f option: 82 83 bash$ hadoop distcp -f hdfs://nn1:8020/srclist \ 84 hdfs://nn2:8020/bar/foo 85 86 Where `srclist` contains 87 88 hdfs://nn1:8020/foo/a 89 hdfs://nn1:8020/foo/b 90 91 When copying from multiple sources, DistCp will abort the copy with an error 92 message if two sources collide, but collisions at the destination are 93 resolved per the [options](#Command_Line_Options) specified. By default, 94 files already existing at the destination are skipped (i.e. not replaced by 95 the source file). A count of skipped files is reported at the end of each 96 job, but it may be inaccurate if a copier failed for some subset of its 97 files, but succeeded on a later attempt. 98 99 It is important that each NodeManager can reach and communicate with both the 100 source and destination file systems. For HDFS, both the source and 101 destination must be running the same version of the protocol or use a 102 backwards-compatible protocol; see [Copying Between Versions] 103 (#Copying_Between_Versions_of_HDFS). 104 105 After a copy, it is recommended that one generates and cross-checks a listing 106 of the source and destination to verify that the copy was truly successful. 107 Since DistCp employs both Map/Reduce and the FileSystem API, issues in or 108 between any of the three could adversely and silently affect the copy. Some 109 have had success running with `-update` enabled to perform a second pass, but 110 users should be acquainted with its semantics before attempting this. 111 112 It's also worth noting that if another client is still writing to a source 113 file, the copy will likely fail. Attempting to overwrite a file being written 114 at the destination should also fail on HDFS. If a source file is (re)moved 115 before it is copied, the copy will fail with a `FileNotFoundException`. 116 117 Please refer to the detailed Command Line Reference for information on all 118 the options available in DistCp. 119 120 $H3 Update and Overwrite 121 122 `-update` is used to copy files from source that don't exist at the target 123 or differ from the target version. `-overwrite` overwrites target-files that 124 exist at the target. 125 126 The Update and Overwrite options warrant special attention since their 127 handling of source-paths varies from the defaults in a very subtle manner. 128 Consider a copy from `/source/first/` and `/source/second/` to `/target/`, 129 where the source paths have the following contents: 130 131 hdfs://nn1:8020/source/first/1 132 hdfs://nn1:8020/source/first/2 133 hdfs://nn1:8020/source/second/10 134 hdfs://nn1:8020/source/second/20 135 136 When DistCp is invoked without `-update` or `-overwrite`, the DistCp defaults 137 would create directories `first/` and `second/`, under `/target`. Thus: 138 139 distcp hdfs://nn1:8020/source/first hdfs://nn1:8020/source/second hdfs://nn2:8020/target 140 141 would yield the following contents in `/target`: 142 143 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/first/1 144 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/first/2 145 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/second/10 146 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/second/20 147 148 When either `-update` or `-overwrite` is specified, the **contents** of the 149 source-directories are copied to target, and not the source directories 150 themselves. Thus: 151 152 distcp -update hdfs://nn1:8020/source/first hdfs://nn1:8020/source/second hdfs://nn2:8020/target 153 154 would yield the following contents in `/target`: 155 156 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/1 157 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/2 158 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/10 159 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/20 160 161 By extension, if both source folders contained a file with the same name 162 (say, `0`), then both sources would map an entry to `/target/0` at the 163 destination. Rather than to permit this conflict, DistCp will abort. 164 165 Now, consider the following copy operation: 166 167 distcp hdfs://nn1:8020/source/first hdfs://nn1:8020/source/second hdfs://nn2:8020/target 168 169 With sources/sizes: 170 171 hdfs://nn1:8020/source/first/1 32 172 hdfs://nn1:8020/source/first/2 32 173 hdfs://nn1:8020/source/second/10 64 174 hdfs://nn1:8020/source/second/20 32 175 176 And destination/sizes: 177 178 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/1 32 179 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/10 32 180 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/20 64 181 182 Will effect: 183 184 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/1 32 185 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/2 32 186 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/10 64 187 hdfs://nn2:8020/target/20 32 188 189 `1` is skipped because the file-length and contents match. `2` is copied 190 because it doesn't exist at the target. `10` and `20` are overwritten since 191 the contents don't match the source. 192 193 If `-update` is used, `1` is skipped because the file-length and contents match. `2` is copied because it doesn’t exist at the target. `10` and `20` are overwritten since the contents don’t match the source. However, if `-append` is additionally used, then only `10` is overwritten (source length less than destination) and `20` is appended with the change in file (if the files match up to the destination's original length). 194 195 If `-overwrite` is used, `1` is overwritten as well. 196 197 $H3 Sync 198 199 `-diff` option syncs files from a source cluster to a target cluster with a 200 snapshot diff. It copies, renames and removes files in the snapshot diff list. 201 202 `-update` option must be included when `-diff` option is in use. 203 204 Most cloud providers don't work well with sync at the moment. 205 206 Usage: 207 208 hadoop distcp -update -diff 209 210 Example: 211 212 hadoop distcp -update -diff snap1 snap2 /src/ /dst/ 213 214 The command above applies changes from snapshot `snap1` to `snap2` 215 (i.e. snapshot diff from `snap1` to `snap2`) in `/src/` to `/dst/`. 216 Obviously, it requires `/src/` to have both snapshots `snap1` and `snap2`. 217 But the destination `/dst/` must also have a snapshot with the same 218 name as ``, in this case `snap1`. The destination `/dst/` 219 should not have new file operations (create, rename, delete) since `snap1`. 220 Note that when this command finishes, a new snapshot `snap2` will NOT be 221 created at `/dst/`. 222 223 `-update` is required to use `-diff` option. 224 225 For instance, in `/src/`, if `1.txt` is added and `2.txt` is deleted after 226 the creation of `snap1` and before creation of `snap2`, the command above 227 will copy `1.txt` from `/src/` to `/dst/` and delete `2.txt` from `/dst/`. 228 229 Sync behavior will be elaborated using experiments below. 230 231 $H4 Experiment 1: Syncing diff of two adjacent snapshots 232 233 Some preparations before we start. 234 235 # Create source and destination directories 236 hdfs dfs -mkdir /src/ /dst/ 237 # Allow snapshot on source 238 hdfs dfsadmin -allowSnapshot /src/ 239 # Create a snapshot (empty one) 240 hdfs dfs -createSnapshot /src/ snap1 241 # Allow snapshot on destination 242 hdfs dfsadmin -allowSnapshot /dst/ 243 # Create a from_snapshot with the same name 244 hdfs dfs -createSnapshot /dst/ snap1 245 246 # Put one text file under /src/ 247 echo "This is the 1st text file." > 1.txt 248 hdfs dfs -put 1.txt /src/ 249 # Create the second snapshot 250 hdfs dfs -createSnapshot /src/ snap2 251 252 # Put another text file under /src/ 253 echo "This is the 2nd text file." > 2.txt 254 hdfs dfs -put 2.txt /src/ 255 # Create the third snapshot 256 hdfs dfs -createSnapshot /src/ snap3 257 258 Then we run distcp sync: 259 260 hadoop distcp -update -diff snap1 snap2 /src/ /dst/ 261 262 The command above should succeed. `1.txt` will be copied from `/src/` to 263 `/dst/`. Again, `-update` option is required. 264 265 If we run the same command again, we will get `DistCp sync failed` exception 266 because the destination has added a new file `1.txt` since `snap1`. That 267 being said, if we remove `1.txt` manually from `/dst/` and run the sync, the 268 command will succeed. 269 270 $H4 Experiment 2: syncing diff of two non-adjacent snapshots 271 272 First do a clean up from Experiment 1. 273 274 hdfs dfs -rm -skipTrash /dst/1.txt 275 276 Run sync command, note the `` has been changed from `snap2` in 277 Experiment 1 to `snap3`. 278 279 hadoop distcp -update -diff snap1 snap3 /src/ /dst/ 280 281 Both `1.txt` and `2.txt` will be copied to `/dst/`. 282 283 $H4 Experiment 3: syncing file delete operation 284 285 Continuing from the end of Experiment 2: 286 287 hdfs dfs -rm -skipTrash /dst/2.txt 288 # Create snap2 at destination, it contains 1.txt 289 hdfs dfs -createSnapshot /dst/ snap2 290 291 # Delete 1.txt from source 292 hdfs dfs -rm -skipTrash /src/1.txt 293 # Create snap4 at source, it only contains 2.txt 294 hdfs dfs -createSnapshot /src/ snap4 295 296 Run sync command now: 297 298 hadoop distcp -update -diff snap2 snap4 /src/ /dst/ 299 300 `2.txt` is copied and `1.txt` is deleted under `/dst/`. 301 302 Note that, though both `/src/` and `/dst/` have snapshot with the same name 303 `snap2`, the snapshots don't need to have the same content. 304 That means, if you have a `1.txt` in `/dst/`'s `snap2` but they have different 305 contents, `1.txt` will still be removed from `/dst/`. 306 The sync command doesn't check the contents of the files that is going to 307 be deleted. It simply follows the snapshot diff list between `` 308 and . 309 310 Also, if we delete `1.txt` from `/dst/` before creating `snap2` on `/dst/` 311 in the steps above, so that `/dst/`'s `snap2` doesn't have `1.txt` before 312 running sync command, the command will still succeed. It won't throw exception 313 while trying to delete `1.txt` from `/dst/` which doesn't exist. 314 315 $H3 raw Namespace Extended Attribute Preservation 316 317 This section only applies to HDFS. 318 319 If the target and all of the source pathnames are in the `/.reserved/raw` 320 hierarchy, then 'raw' namespace extended attributes will be preserved. 321 'raw' xattrs are used by the system for internal functions such as encryption 322 meta data. They are only visible to users when accessed through the 323 `/.reserved/raw` hierarchy. 324 325 raw xattrs are preserved based solely on whether /.reserved/raw prefixes are 326 supplied. The -p (preserve, see below) flag does not impact preservation of 327 raw xattrs. 328 329 To prevent raw xattrs from being preserved, simply do not use the 330 `/.reserved/raw` prefix on any of the source and target paths. 331 332 If the `/.reserved/raw `prefix is specified on only a subset of the source and 333 target paths, an error will be displayed and a non-0 exit code returned. 334 335 Command Line Options 336 -------------------- 337 338 | Flag | Description | Notes | 339 | ----------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------- | 340 | `-p[rbugpcaxte]` | Preserve r: replication number b: block size u: user g: group p: permission c: checksum-type a: ACL x: XAttr t: timestamp e: erasure coding policy | When `-update` is specified, status updates will **not** be synchronized unless the file sizes also differ (i.e. unless the file is re-created). If -pa is specified, DistCp preserves the permissions also because ACLs are a super-set of permissions. The option -pr is only valid if both source and target directory are not erasure coded. | 341 | `-i` | Ignore failures | As explained in the Appendix, this option will keep more accurate statistics about the copy than the default case. It also preserves logs from failed copies, which can be valuable for debugging. Finally, a failing map will not cause the job to fail before all splits are attempted. | 342 | `-log ` | Write logs to \ | DistCp keeps logs of each file it attempts to copy as map output. If a map fails, the log output will not be retained if it is re-executed. | 343 | `-v` | Log additional info (path, size) in the SKIP/COPY log | This option can only be used with -log option. | 344 | `-m ` | Maximum number of simultaneous copies | Specify the number of maps to copy data. Note that more maps may not necessarily improve throughput. | 345 | `-overwrite` | Overwrite destination | If a map fails and `-i` is not specified, all the files in the split, not only those that failed, will be recopied. As discussed in the Usage documentation, it also changes the semantics for generating destination paths, so users should use this carefully. | 346 | `-update` | Overwrite if source and destination differ in size, blocksize, or checksum | As noted in the preceding, this is not a "sync" operation. The criteria examined are the source and destination file sizes, blocksizes, and checksums; if they differ, the source file replaces the destination file. As discussed in the Usage documentation, it also changes the semantics for generating destination paths, so users should use this carefully. | 347 | `-append` | Incremental copy of file with same name but different length | If the source file is greater in length than the destination file, the checksum of the common length part is compared. If the checksum matches, only the difference is copied using read and append functionalities. The -append option only works with `-update` without `-skipcrccheck` | 348 | `-f ` | Use list at \ as src list | This is equivalent to listing each source on the command line. The `urilist_uri` list should be a fully qualified URI. | 349 | `-filters` | The path to a file containing a list of pattern strings, one string per line, such that paths matching the pattern will be excluded from the copy. | Support regular expressions specified by java.util.regex.Pattern. | 350 | `-filelimit ` | Limit the total number of files to be <= n | **Deprecated!** Ignored in the new DistCp. | 351 | `-sizelimit ` | Limit the total size to be <= n bytes | **Deprecated!** Ignored in the new DistCp. | 352 | `-delete` | Delete the files existing in the dst but not in src | The deletion is done by FS Shell. So the trash will be used, if it is enable. Delete is applicable only with update or overwrite options. | 353 | `-strategy {dynamic|uniformsize}` | Choose the copy-strategy to be used in DistCp. | By default, uniformsize is used. (i.e. Maps are balanced on the total size of files copied by each map. Similar to legacy.) If "dynamic" is specified, `DynamicInputFormat` is used instead. (This is described in the Architecture section, under InputFormats.) | 354 | `-bandwidth` | Specify bandwidth per map, in MB/second. | Each map will be restricted to consume only the specified bandwidth. This is not always exact. The map throttles back its bandwidth consumption during a copy, such that the **net** bandwidth used tends towards the specified value. | 355 | `-atomic {-tmp }` | Specify atomic commit, with optional tmp directory. | `-atomic` instructs DistCp to copy the source data to a temporary target location, and then move the temporary target to the final-location atomically. Data will either be available at final target in a complete and consistent form, or not at all. Optionally, `-tmp` may be used to specify the location of the tmp-target. If not specified, a default is chosen. **Note:** tmp_dir must be on the final target cluster. | 356 | `-async` | Run DistCp asynchronously. Quits as soon as the Hadoop Job is launched. | The Hadoop Job-id is logged, for tracking. | 357 | `-diff ` | Use snapshot diff report between given two snapshots to identify the difference between source and target, and apply the diff to the target to make it in sync with source. | This option is valid only with `-update` option and the following conditions should be satisfied.
  1. Both the source and the target FileSystem must be DistributedFileSystem.
  2. Two snapshots `` and `` have been created on the source FS, and `` is older than ``.
  3. The target has the same snapshot ``. No changes have been made on the target since `` was created, thus `` has the same content as the current state of the target. All the files/directories in the target are the same with source's ``.
| 358 | `-rdiff ` | Use snapshot diff report between given two snapshots to identify what has been changed on the target since the snapshot `` was created on the target, and apply the diff reversely to the target, and copy modified files from the source's ``, to make the target the same as ``. | This option is valid only with `-update` option and the following conditions should be satisfied.
  1. Both the source and the target FileSystem must be DistributedFileSystem. The source and the target can be two different clusters/paths, or they can be exactly the same cluster/path. In the latter case, modified files are copied from target's `` to target's current state).
  2. Two snapshots `` and `` have been created on the target FS, and `` is older than ``. No change has been made on target since `` was created on the target.

| 359 | `-numListstatusThreads` | Number of threads to use for building file listing | At most 40 threads. | 360 | `-skipcrccheck` | Whether to skip CRC checks between source and target paths. | | 361 | `-blocksperchunk ` | Number of blocks per chunk. These arguments include: 390 391 * Source-paths 392 * Target location 393 * Copy options (e.g. whether to update-copy, overwrite, which 394 file-attributes to preserve, etc.) 395 396 * Orchestrating the copy operation by: 397 398 * Invoking the copy-listing-generator to create the list of files to be 399 copied. 400 * Setting up and launching the Hadoop Map-Reduce Job to carry out the 401 copy. 402 * Based on the options, either returning a handle to the Hadoop MR Job 403 immediately, or waiting till completion. 404 405 The parser-elements are exercised only from the command-line (or if 406 DistCp::run() is invoked). The DistCp class may also be used 407 programmatically, by constructing the DistCpOptions object, and initializing 408 a DistCp object appropriately. 409 410 $H3 Copy-listing Generator 411 412 The copy-listing-generator classes are responsible for creating the list of 413 files/directories to be copied from source. They examine the contents of the 414 source-paths (files/directories, including wild-cards), and record all paths 415 that need copy into a SequenceFile, for consumption by the DistCp Hadoop 416 Job. The main classes in this module include: 417 418 1. `CopyListing`: The interface that should be implemented by any 419 copy-listing-generator implementation. Also provides the factory method by 420 which the concrete CopyListing implementation is chosen. 421 2. `SimpleCopyListing`: An implementation of `CopyListing` that accepts multiple 422 source paths (files/directories), and recursively lists all the individual 423 files and directories under each, for copy. 424 3. `GlobbedCopyListing`: Another implementation of `CopyListing` that expands 425 wild-cards in the source paths. 426 4. `FileBasedCopyListing`: An implementation of `CopyListing` that reads the 427 source-path list from a specified file. 428 429 Based on whether a source-file-list is specified in the DistCpOptions, the 430 source-listing is generated in one of the following ways: 431 432 1. If there's no source-file-list, the `GlobbedCopyListing` is used. All 433 wild-cards are expanded, and all the expansions are forwarded to the 434 SimpleCopyListing, which in turn constructs the listing (via recursive 435 descent of each path). 436 2. If a source-file-list is specified, the `FileBasedCopyListing` is used. 437 Source-paths are read from the specified file, and then forwarded to the 438 `GlobbedCopyListing`. The listing is then constructed as described above. 439 440 One may customize the method by which the copy-listing is constructed by 441 providing a custom implementation of the CopyListing interface. The behaviour 442 of DistCp differs here from the legacy DistCp, in how paths are considered 443 for copy. 444 445 One may also customize the filtering of files which shouldn't be copied 446 by passing the current supported implementation of CopyFilter interface 447 or a new implementation can be written. This can be specified by setting the 448 `distcp.filters.class` in the DistCpOptions: 449 450 1. `distcp.filters.class` to "RegexCopyFilter". If you are using this implementation, 451 you will have to pass along "CopyFilter" `distcp.filters.file` which contains the 452 regex used for filtering. Support regular expressions specified by 453 java.util.regex.Pattern. 454 2. `distcp.filters.class` to "RegexpInConfigurationFilter". If you are using this 455 implementation, you will have to pass along the regex also using 456 `distcp.exclude-file-regex` parameter in "DistCpOptions". Support regular 457 expressions specified by java.util.regex.Pattern. This is a more dynamic approach 458 as compared to "RegexCopyFilter". 459 3. `distcp.filters.class` to "TrueCopyFilter". This is used as a default 460 implementation if none of the above options are specified. 461 462 The legacy implementation only lists those paths that must definitely be 463 copied on to target. E.g. if a file already exists at the target (and 464 `-overwrite` isn't specified), the file isn't even considered in the 465 MapReduce Copy Job. Determining this during setup (i.e. before the MapReduce 466 Job) involves file-size and checksum-comparisons that are potentially 467 time-consuming. 468 469 The new DistCp postpones such checks until the MapReduce Job, thus reducing 470 setup time. Performance is enhanced further since these checks are 471 parallelized across multiple maps. 472 473 $H3 InputFormats and MapReduce Components 474 475 The InputFormats and MapReduce components are responsible for the actual copy 476 of files and directories from the source to the destination path. The 477 listing-file created during copy-listing generation is consumed at this 478 point, when the copy is carried out. The classes of interest here include: 479 480 * **UniformSizeInputFormat:** 481 This implementation of org.apache.hadoop.mapreduce.InputFormat provides 482 equivalence with Legacy DistCp in balancing load across maps. The aim of 483 the UniformSizeInputFormat is to make each map copy roughly the same number 484 of bytes. Apropos, the listing file is split into groups of paths, such 485 that the sum of file-sizes in each InputSplit is nearly equal to every 486 other map. The splitting isn't always perfect, but its trivial 487 implementation keeps the setup-time low. 488 489 * **DynamicInputFormat and DynamicRecordReader:** 490 The DynamicInputFormat implements `org.apache.hadoop.mapreduce.InputFormat`, 491 and is new to DistCp. The listing-file is split into several "chunk-files", 492 the exact number of chunk-files being a multiple of the number of maps 493 requested for in the Hadoop Job. Each map task is "assigned" one of the 494 chunk-files (by renaming the chunk to the task's id), before the Job is 495 launched. 496 Paths are read from each chunk using the `DynamicRecordReader`, and 497 processed in the CopyMapper. After all the paths in a chunk are processed, 498 the current chunk is deleted and a new chunk is acquired. The process 499 continues until no more chunks are available. 500 This "dynamic" approach allows faster map-tasks to consume more paths than 501 slower ones, thus speeding up the DistCp job overall. 502 503 * **CopyMapper:** 504 This class implements the physical file-copy. The input-paths are checked 505 against the input-options (specified in the Job's Configuration), to 506 determine whether a file needs copy. A file will be copied only if at least 507 one of the following is true: 508 509 * A file with the same name doesn't exist at target. 510 * A file with the same name exists at target, but has a different file 511 size. 512 * A file with the same name exists at target, but has a different 513 checksum, and `-skipcrccheck` isn't mentioned. 514 * A file with the same name exists at target, but `-overwrite` is 515 specified. 516 * A file with the same name exists at target, but differs in block-size 517 (and block-size needs to be preserved. 518 519 * **CopyCommitter:** This class is responsible for the commit-phase of the 520 DistCp job, including: 521 522 * Preservation of directory-permissions (if specified in the options) 523 * Clean-up of temporary-files, work-directories, etc. 524 525 Appendix 526 -------- 527 528 $H3 Map sizing 529 530 By default, DistCp makes an attempt to size each map comparably so that each 531 copies roughly the same number of bytes. Note that files are the finest level 532 of granularity, so increasing the number of simultaneous copiers (i.e. maps) 533 may not always increase the number of simultaneous copies nor the overall 534 throughput. 535 536 The new DistCp also provides a strategy to "dynamically" size maps, allowing 537 faster data-nodes to copy more bytes than slower nodes. Using `-strategy 538 dynamic` (explained in the Architecture), rather than to assign a fixed set 539 of source-files to each map-task, files are instead split into several sets. 540 The number of sets exceeds the number of maps, usually by a factor of 2-3. 541 Each map picks up and copies all files listed in a chunk. When a chunk is 542 exhausted, a new chunk is acquired and processed, until no more chunks 543 remain. 544 545 By not assigning a source-path to a fixed map, faster map-tasks (i.e. 546 data-nodes) are able to consume more chunks, and thus copy more data, than 547 slower nodes. While this distribution isn't uniform, it is fair with regard 548 to each mapper's capacity. 549 550 The dynamic-strategy is implemented by the `DynamicInputFormat`. It provides 551 superior performance under most conditions. 552 553 Tuning the number of maps to the size of the source and destination clusters, 554 the size of the copy, and the available bandwidth is recommended for 555 long-running and regularly run jobs. 556 557 $H3 Copying Between Versions of HDFS 558 559 For copying between two different major versions of Hadoop (e.g. between 1.X 560 and 2.X), one will usually use WebHdfsFileSystem. Unlike the previous 561 HftpFileSystem, as webhdfs is available for both read and write operations, 562 DistCp can be run on both source and destination cluster. 563 Remote cluster is specified as `webhdfs://:`. 564 When copying between same major versions of Hadoop cluster (e.g. between 2.X 565 and 2.X), use hdfs protocol for better performance. 566 567 $H3 Secure Copy over the wire with distcp 568 Use the "`swebhdfs://`" scheme when webhdfs is secured with SSL. The JAR containing the object store implementation is on the classpath, 589 along with all of its dependencies. 590 1. Unless the JAR automatically registers its bundled filesystem clients, 591 the configuration may need to be modified to state the class which 592 implements the filesystem schema. All of the ASF's own object store clients 593 are self-registering. 594 1. The relevant object store access credentials must be available in the cluster 595 configuration, or be otherwise available in all cluster hosts. 596 597 DistCp can be used to upload data 598 599 ```bash 600 hadoop distcp -direct hdfs://nn1:8020/datasets/set1 s3a://bucket/datasets/set1 601 ``` 602 603 To download data 604 605 ```bash 606 hadoop distcp s3a://bucket/generated/results hdfs://nn1:8020/results 607 ``` 608 609 To copy data between object stores 610 611 ```bash 612 hadoop distcp s3a://bucket/generated/results \ 613 wasb://updates@example.blob.core.windows.net 614 ``` 615 616 And do copy data within an object store 617 618 ```bash 619 hadoop distcp wasb://updates@example.blob.core.windows.net/current \ 620 wasb://updates@example.blob.core.windows.net/old 621 ``` 622 623 And to use `-update` to only copy changed files. 624 625 ```bash 626 hadoop distcp -update -numListstatusThreads 20 \ 627 swift://history.cluster1/2016 \ 628 hdfs://nn1:8020/history/2016 629 ``` 630 631 Because object stores are slow to list files, consider setting the `-numListstatusThreads` option when performing a `-update` operation 632 on a large directory tree (the limit is 40 threads). 633 634 When `DistCp -update` is used with object stores, 635 generally only the modification time and length of the individual files are compared, 636 not any checksums. The fact that most object stores do have valid timestamps 637 for directories is irrelevant; only the file timestamps are compared. 638 However, it is important to have the clock of the client computers close 639 to that of the infrastructure, so that timestamps are consistent between 640 the client/HDFS cluster and that of the object store. Otherwise, changed files may be 641 missed/copied too often. 642 643 **Notes** 644 645 * The `-atomic` option causes a rename of the temporary data, so significantly 646 increases the time to commit work at the end of the operation. Furthermore, 647 as Object Stores other than (optionally) `wasb://` do not offer atomic renames of directories 648 the `-atomic` operation doesn't actually deliver what is promised. *Avoid*. 649 650 * The `-append` option is not supported. 651 652 * The `-diff` and `rdiff` options are not supported 653 654 * CRC checking will not be performed, irrespective of the value of the `-skipCrc` 655 flag. 656 657 * All `-p` options, including those to preserve permissions, user and group information, attributes 658 checksums and replication are generally ignored. The `wasb://` connector will 659 preserve the information, but not enforce the permissions. 660 661 * Some object store connectors offer an option for in-memory buffering of 662 output —for example the S3A connector. Using such option while copying 663 large files may trigger some form of out of memory event, 664 be it a heap overflow or a YARN container termination. 665 This is particularly common if the network bandwidth 666 between the cluster and the object store is limited (such as when working 667 with remote object stores). It is best to disable/avoid such options and 668 rely on disk buffering. 669 670 * Copy operations within a single object store still take place in the Hadoop cluster 671 —even when the object store implements a more efficient COPY operation internally 672 673 That is, an operation such as 674 675 hadoop distcp s3a://bucket/datasets/set1 s3a://bucket/datasets/set2 676 677 Copies each byte down to the Hadoop worker nodes and back to the 678 bucket. As well as being slow, it means that charges may be incurred. 679 680 * The `-direct` option can be used to write to object store target paths directly, 681 avoiding the potentially very expensive temporary file rename operations that would 682 otherwise occur. 683 684 Frequently Asked Questions 685 -------------------------- 686 687 1. **Why does -update not create the parent source-directory under a pre-existing target directory?** 688 The behaviour of `-update` and `-overwrite` is described in detail in the 689 Usage section of this document. In short, if either option is used with a 690 pre-existing destination directory, the **contents** of each source 691 directory is copied over, rather than the source-directory itself. This 692 behaviour is consistent with the legacy DistCp implementation as well. 693 694 2. **How does the new DistCp differ in semantics from the Legacy DistCp?** 695 696 * Files that are skipped during copy used to also have their 697 file-attributes (permissions, owner/group info, etc.) unchanged, when 698 copied with Legacy DistCp. These are now updated, even if the file-copy 699 is skipped. 700 * Empty root directories among the source-path inputs were not created at 701 the target, in Legacy DistCp. These are now created. 702 703 3. **Why does the new DistCp use more maps than legacy DistCp?** 704 Legacy DistCp works by figuring out what files need to be actually copied 705 to target before the copy-job is launched, and then launching as many maps 706 as required for copy. So if a majority of the files need to be skipped 707 (because they already exist, for example), fewer maps will be needed. As a 708 consequence, the time spent in setup (i.e. before the M/R job) is higher. 709 The new DistCp calculates only the contents of the source-paths. It 710 doesn't try to filter out what files can be skipped. That decision is put 711 off till the M/R job runs. This is much faster (vis-a-vis execution-time), 712 but the number of maps launched will be as specified in the `-m` option, 713 or 20 (default) if unspecified. 714 715 4. **Why does DistCp not run faster when more maps are specified?** 716 At present, the smallest unit of work for DistCp is a file. i.e., a file 717 is processed by only one map. Increasing the number of maps to a value 718 exceeding the number of files would yield no performance benefit. The 719 number of maps launched would equal the number of files. 720 721 5. **Why does DistCp run out of memory?** 722 If the number of individual files/directories being copied from the source 723 path(s) is extremely large (e.g. 1,000,000 paths), DistCp might run out of 724 memory while determining the list of paths for copy. This is not unique to 725 the new DistCp implementation. 726 To get around this, consider changing the `-Xmx` JVM heap-size parameters, 727 as follows: 728 729 bash$ export HADOOP_CLIENT_OPTS="-Xms64m -Xmx1024m" 730 bash$ hadoop distcp /source /target 731
